title: DC Mayor's Office Hosts Diwali Celebration on Friday, November 6
excerpt: The MOAPIA 2026 Diwali Celebration is at 899 North Capitol Street NE at 6 p.m. ET, listed as free, opening the capital's Diwali weekend.
body:
• Washington, DC's Mayor's Office on Asian and Pacific Islander Affairs (MOAPIA) hosts its 2026 Diwali Celebration on Friday, November 6, at 6:00 p.m. ET.
  • The venue is 899 North Capitol Street NE, Washington, DC 20002, and the Eventbrite listing by the Executive Office of Mayor Muriel Bowser lists the event as free.
  • Diwali itself falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026 — the Mayor's Office celebration opens the festival weekend in the capital.
  • Reserve through the Mayor's Office Eventbrite page before going; the listing does not state an end time.

Washington's official Diwali celebration returns on Friday, November 6, when the Mayor's Office on Asian and Pacific Islander Affairs (MOAPIA) hosts the MOAPIA 2026 Diwali Celebration at 899 North Capitol Street NE. Eventbrite listings from the Executive Office of Mayor Muriel Bowser show the event at 6:00 p.m., listed as free, at the same North Capitol Street address the Mayor's Office uses for its community events.

Plan Your Visit

  • Date: Friday, November 6, 2026
  • Time: 6:00 p.m. ET (the listing does not state an end time)
  • Venue: Mayor's Office community event space
  • Address: 899 North Capitol Street NE, Washington, DC 20002
  • Admission: Free, per the Eventbrite listing
  • Official page: Executive Office of Mayor Muriel Bowser on Eventbrite — the MOAPIA Diwali Celebration is listed under the office's upcoming events

An official celebration, in a city that marks Diwali at scale

MOAPIA's Diwali reception is a long-running fixture of the District's civic calendar: the office has hosted an annual Diwali celebration for the city's Hindu, Sikh, Jain and Buddhist communities for years, traditionally with a lamp-lighting ceremony and cultural performances. What is on this year's programme has not been detailed in the listing beyond the date, time and venue, so attendees should check the official Eventbrite page closer to Friday for any programme or registration update.

The timing is deliberate. Diwali's main day this year is Sunday, November 8, so the Mayor's Office event opens a festival weekend in the capital rather than competing with family and temple celebrations on the day itself.

Other events nearby

Also on Friday evening, the Smithsonian's National Museum of Asian Art holds its Asia After Dark Diwali festival, with classical music performances, a DJ dance party and curator talks, Washingtonian's November culture guide reported — free, with registration encouraged. The two events are separate: the Smithsonian's is at the National Museum of Asian Art on Independence Avenue SW, across the National Mall from the MOAPIA venue.
